item.title: [ZEPPELIN-2515] After 100 minutes R process quits silently and spark.r interpreter becomes unresponsive.
item.description:
On Zeppelin 0.7.1, an R process quits/crash/gets killed with no apparent reason and Spark session remains alive, so %spark.r interpreter needs to be restarted. On 0.7.0 restarting the interpreter doesn't always work, so Zeppelin requires a full restart.

These are the steps I followed to produce this behaviour:

1) Enable log4j debug properties.

2) Start a brand new instance of zeppelin issuing:
service zeppelin stop
service zeppelin start

3) Open an existing notebook or create a new one and execute this block of code:

%spark.r
2+2

4) Wait for 3) to finish and close the browser. The zeppelin log should report something like this:

INFO [2017-05-08 12:26:15,879] (

{qtp423031029-60}

NotebookServer.java[onClose]:363) - Closed connection to 127.0.0.1 : 33798. (1001) null

5) Wait several minutes (usually 30 minutes or more) without using zeppelin and without reconnecting via browser and at a certain point R will quit. The interpreter log file should contain something similar to these lines:

DEBUG [2017-05-08 13:08:00,187] (

{Exec Stream Pumper} InterpreterOutputStream.java[processLine]:72) - Interpreter output:Error in handleErrors(returnStatus, conn) :
DEBUG [2017-05-08 13:08:00,188] ({Exec Stream Pumper}

InterpreterOutputStream.java[processLine]:72) - Interpreter output: No status is returned. Java SparkR backend might have failed.
DEBUG [2017-05-08 13:08:00,188] (

{Exec Stream Pumper} InterpreterOutputStream.java[processLine]:72) - Interpreter output:Calls: <Anonymous> -> invokeJava -> handleErrors
DEBUG [2017-05-08 13:08:00,188] ({Exec Stream Pumper}

InterpreterOutputStream.java[processLine]:72) - Interpreter output:Execution halted

6) If you repeat the previouse steps from 3) to 5), R will quit again after at least 30 minutes.

The machine running Zeppelin is a server and the client is located on another machine.
The error is reproducible with Zeppelin 0.7.0 and 0.7.1 using Spark 2.1.0 and 2.1.1 (latest available version).

This issue has been discussed here:
https://lists.apache.org/thread.html/17d8bbea0b755a9cf866a6d78909493d63b09bfa92a477bc0e28bc1c@%3Cusers.zeppelin.apache.org%3E

comments.comment:
One big find (tested with Spark 2.1.0 and 2.1.1): the elapsed time between start and stop time of the R process is 100 minutes (1 hour and 40 minutes). It doesn't matter when you disconnect or close the browser. This leads me to think that there's a timeout occuring somewhere. I tried pushing these Spark options in conf/spark-defaults.conf but the timeout still occurs at 100 minutes:
spark.r.heartBeatInterval 10
spark.r.backendConnectionTimeout 1000000

I don't know if the timeout occurs due to Spark configuration or to some Zeppelin "sort of keep-alive" behaviour.

Probably I have found the cause if this issue.

Starting from Spark 2.1.0 it's possible to configure the RBackend timeout in two ways:
1) add this line to spark-env.sh:
SPARKR_BACKEND_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT="1000000000"
2) add this line to spark-defaults.conf:
spark.r.backendConnectionTimeout 1000000

These settings are being read by SparkR library through the function connectBackend(hostname, port, timeout) defined in spark/R/pkg/R/client.R
Before Spark 2.1.0, timeout default value was 6000 and ZeppelinR explicitly sets it to 6000 in zeppelin/spark/src/main/resources/R/zeppelin_sparkr.R this way:
SparkR:::connectBackend("localhost", port, 6000) # WRONG

The third parameter overrides the new timeout behaviour defined since Spark 2.1.0 and overrides the values set in steps 1) and 2), so the R session will be killed always after 6000 seconds.

The solution consists of don't specifying any timeout:
SparkR:::connectBackend("localhost", port) # CORRECT

Can someone please edit the code and commit it?

Thank you all
I can make a PR but I don't have any knowledge for testing it. Please help to review though

I can test it. PR stands for Push Request? Tell me what to do (git pull etc)
Thank you

connectBackend <- function(hostname, port, timeout) doesn't specify a default value for parameter timeout, so any call made outside Spark need to specify it, overriding the parameters passed by user in spark-env.sh or in spark-defaults.conf.

Spark sets the default timeout from sparkR.sparkContext() and then passes it to connectBackend(hostname, port, timeout) directly. IMHO this is wrong. This forces softwares like Zeppelin to identify a proper way to assign a default value. One possible solution is to set it from inside SparkR:::connectBackend().

For example, if this solution won't be adopted by Spark community, Zeppelin should read spark-env.sh and spark-defaults.conf to get SPARKR_BACKEND_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT and spark.r.backendConnectionTimeout values as the default timeout value. This doesn't make sense at all.

Another solution is to create a similar configuration variable in zeppelin-env.sh. This makes more sense to me, but it will override the timeout value set in spark-env.sh and spark-defaults.conf.
pietrop You can set SPARKR_BACKEND_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT and spark.r.backendConnectionTimeout into your interpreter tabs.
